RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-female panel is not evidence of bias; composition typically reflects departmental availability, committee rotations, or subject specializations. 

Academic appointments rarely depend solely on paper counts or degree completion status. Hiring committees frequently weigh department-specific curricular needs, where practical industry experience or a specialized niche may outweigh additional academic publications. Interview performance, teaching demonstrations, and institutional fit are also heavily weighted.

Raising the panel’s gender without concrete evidence of procedural irregularities or discriminatory conduct will almost certainly be viewed as bad faith, harming your professional reputation. Instead, send a polite follow-up inquiring purely about constructive feedback on your interview and how you can strengthen future applications for similar roles.
